localBiteReport: Reports from the past week around Choctawhatchee Bay suggest inshore action has been decent but somewhat inconsistent on quality fish. A charter review on FishingBooker dated approximately November 15 noted two keeper redfish caught by working bait under a bridge near the bay. The CaptainExperiences Choctawhatchee Bay guide feed (reported about one week ago) noted the bite has been good for numbers but slightly slower on larger fish, with live bait producing best in the early morning and soft plastics effective throughout the day — consistent with mid-November cooling patterns. Water temperature at this location is currently 69°F. As a general November pattern for the bay, sheepshead are known to pick up around bridge structure as water cools, while redfish remain available on the flats and in deeper holes, and speckled trout fishing typically stays solid.
